report:
### Conclusion
Your sister’s view is supported by clinical evidence: **chlorhexidine-alcohol skin preparation reduces surgical-site infections (SSIs) compared with iodine-alcohol** (and aqueous povidone-iodine) before cesarean delivery.

### Key Evidence
* **Landmark Clinical Trial:** A randomized controlled trial published in *The New England Journal of Medicine* directly compared chlorhexidine-alcohol to iodine-alcohol skin antisepsis in 1,147 patients undergoing cesarean delivery. Chlorhexidine-alcohol significantly lowered SSI rates (4.0% vs. 7.3%), achieving roughly a 45% reduction in infection risk.
* **Systematic Reviews & Meta-Analyses:** Synthesised evidence from multiple trials demonstrates that alcohol-based chlorhexidine reduces superficial and deep incisional infections more effectively than iodine-based preparations. Network meta-analyses rank alcohol-based 2% chlorhexidine as having the highest probability of preventing SSIs after cesarean delivery.
* **Guideline Recommendations:** Major health organizations and consensus groups—including the CDC, WHO, and ERAS Society—recommend alcohol-based chlorhexidine gluconate as the preferred abdominal skin antiseptic prior to cesarean delivery.

### Cited Sources
1. *New England Journal of Medicine* (Randomized Trial): https://www.nejm.org/doi/full/10.1056/NEJMoa1511048
2. *PubMed* (Systematic Review & Meta-Analysis): https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/30184558/
3. *ScienceDirect* (Network Meta-Analysis of RCTs): https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/abs/pii/S0195670124001282
4. *American Journal of Obstetrics & Gynecology* (ERAS Guidelines): https://www.ajog.org/article/S0002-9378(18)30658-6/fulltext
